findings.justification: E5 is from the 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (EXACT_MATCH period). It shows operating margin for 2025 was 32%, which does not exceed 30% but equals 32%. The assertion claims it 'exceeded 30%', which is technically satisfied since 32% > 30%. However, the table shows the operating margin was exactly 32%, not exceeding 30% in the sense of being substantially above it. Actually, 32% does exceed 30%, so this ENTAILS the assertion.

E7 and E8 are XBRL facts for the exact period (2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, EXACT_MATCH). Operating income was $129,039 million and revenue was $402,836 million. Operating margin = 129,039 / 402,836 = 0.3203 = 32.03%, which exceeds 30%.
E11 is a derived metric for operating margin at 2025-12-31 for the annual period (COMPATIBLE_AFTER_VERIFIED_DERIVATION). The value is 0.3203 or 32.03%, which exceeds 30%.

E1 shows operating margin for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was 31%. This is a quarterly figure (period_status MISMATCH), not the full fiscal year 2025, so it does not decide the annual claim.
E2 shows operating margin for the three months ended June 30, 2025 was 32%. This is a quarterly figure (period_status MISMATCH), not the full fiscal year 2025, so it does not decide the annual claim.

findings.key_quote: we may experience downward pressure on our operating margin in the future
findings.justification: E4 discusses potential future downward pressure on operating margin. This is forward-looking risk disclosure, not a statement of what the operating margin was for fiscal year 2025.

findings.key_quote: our historical revenue growth rate and historical operating margin may not be indicative of our future performance
findings.justification: E17 discusses factors that may affect future margins and notes that historical margins may not be indicative of future performance. This is context about margin trends and risks, not a statement of the actual FY2025 operating margin level.
